# 2026 season backtest

Every forecast below was made with only the games that had already been played, then graded against what actually happened.

*Generated by `python scripts/backtest.py 2026`. Regenerate after refreshing the data with `scripts/update_recent_games.py`, or after changing the model parameters in `forecast.py`.*

> **Leakage check passed.** Re-forecasting from a history truncated before weeks 1, 8, 15 and 22 reproduced the same probabilities exactly, so no future result influenced any prediction.

## How the three forecasters finished

| Forecaster | Straight up | Win rate | Confidence pool | Pool share | Brier points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elo | 10-6 | 62.5% | 89 / 136 | 65.4% | 30.3 |
| Vegas | 12-4 | 75.0% | 101 / 136 | 74.3% | 55.2 |
| Combined | 10-6 | 62.5% | 97 / 136 | 71.3% | 47.1 |

**Vegas won the confidence pool**, and **Vegas picked the most winners outright** (12-4). Elo trailed Vegas by 12 pool points (8.8 percentage points) and 25 Brier points.

## Week by week

| Week | Games | Elo | Vegas | Combined | Elo pool | Vegas pool | Pot |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Week 1 | 16 | 10-6 | 12-4 | 10-6 | 89 | 101 | 136 |

Ignoring the playoff rounds, which are too small to compare, Elo's best week was Week 1 (89 of 136 pool points, 10-6 straight up) and its worst was Week 1 (89 of 136, 10-6).

Elo out-scored Vegas in 0 of 1 weeks, so the season gap is not one bad afternoon - the market was ahead most weeks.

## Is Elo's confidence honest?

When the model says 75%, does the favourite win about 75% of the time?

| Stated confidence | Games | Model said | Actually won |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50-60% | 8 | 55.7% | 62.5% |
| 60-70% | 6 | 64.2% | 66.7% |
| 70-80% | 2 | 72.9% | 50.0% |

Same question for Vegas:

| Stated confidence | Games | Market said | Actually won |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50-60% | 8 | 56.1% | 75.0% |
| 60-70% | 4 | 64.7% | 75.0% |
| 70-80% | 4 | 75.7% | 75.0% |
